messages:
zara: Heads-up  a pilot customer asked for a single-chat call that can orchestrate multiple 'actions' (model calls, external HTTP steps, embeddings). Key asks: declare dependencies, per-action timeouts, optional vs required, and ability to return partial results when optional steps fail.

noah: Can we get concrete examples they care about?

zara: Example A: run a vector search -> rerank results -> compute embeddings for top 5. Example B: document pipeline: chunk -> embed -> index -> signal success to downstream webhook. They want retries for flaky index endpoints and a best-effort UI experience when some parts fail.

lee: From runtime: we need to know max fanout, whether to support arbitrary DAGs or restrict to shallow graphs, and how KV cache / model context flows between dependent actions.

sana: Product constraints: do not change existing function-calling surface; expose action-level telemetry (latency, tokens, status) and keep a single correlation_id for a plan. Beta behind flag.

zara: Proposed minimal API: POST /v1/chat/plan with body that includes messages + actions array. Each action: id, kind, input, deps: [], required: true|false, timeout_ms, retry_policy: attempts/backoff_ms, idempotent: true|false, merge_strategy (optional). Response: { completion_text, action_results: { id: { status, output, error, metrics } } }

noah: Add merge_strategy options for similar outputs from multiple actions: concat|mean|top_k. Also allow on_error fallback: { fallback_action_id } or abort_flow.

lee: Runtime MVP notes: restrict DAG depth <= 2 or 3 to simplify scheduler. Fanout default <= 6. Parallelizable actions scheduled on separate workers; dependent actions run after all deps succeed (or depending on required flag). Global request timeout enforced; per-action soft timeout returns status timed_out and any partial output.

sana: Retry semantics: only retry when idempotent=true and error is transient (5xx/network). Retries bounded by retry_policy and global timeout. For non-idempotent actions, surface error immediately; caller can declare fallback behavior.

zara: Observability: action-level metrics must include attempts, latency_ms, tokens_consumed (if model call), worker_pool, and trace_id. Also log reason for retries and redacted request inputs.

noah: Security: external HTTP actions require org-level allowlist and belong to a restricted permission flag. Redact secrets from logs and disallow raw private keys in action inputs.

lee: Cost implications: document how actions map to billing (per model token for model calls, per-embedding unit for embed actions, external calls billed as infra). Provide examples in docs showing cost estimate for typical pipelines.

sana: UX: provide SDK helpers that convert a high-level pipeline into actions array, and helper to interpret action_results for UI (showing which actions succeeded vs timed_out). Also sample best-effort UI patterns.

zara: Launch criteria (candidate): spec + OpenAPI examples, SDK samples (py/js), telemetry dashboards for action-level KPIs, E2E tests with flaky backends, security review, beta feature flag + pilot.

noah: Edge cases to encode in spec PR: cycles => reject with 400 + helpful error; duplicate ids => reject; oversized plans (downstream calls > 100) => reject or require special quota; optional actions failing => include partial results and mark overall response as partial_success.

lee: Implementation plan: prototype scheduler that accepts shallow DAGs and coalesces embed calls when possible. Use existing batching for model calls. Add ticket to avoid copying KV across workers (use shared cache).

sana: Admin controls: org-level settings for max fanout, allow external actions, and default retry limits. Also telemetry retention options.

zara: I'll open the spec PR with JSON examples and a few canonical pipelines. Noah + Lee, please flag any implementation blockers. I'll tag the pilot customer once we have a beta build.

ci-bot: CI: branch feat/plan-exec started build (queued).

noah: +1

lee: +1

sana: Will add docs outline and sample UI snippets by EOD.
